messages:
nina (devex): Heads-up: customer TICKET-1198 onboarding hit a blocker. Async Python client fails through corporate proxy on Windows when talking to a Dedicated (VPC) endpoint. Sync (requests) works fine.

nina (devex): Short error they see: 
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

leo (py-sdk): Classic. Which CA handling did they try? REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE vs env?

nina (devex): They set REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE=C:\\corp\\proxy_ca.pem and REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://dedicated.customer.redwood.ai and http_proxy=http://corp-proxy:8080. No luck.

omar (infra): On Windows the store vs file confusion is frequent. Also aiohttp won't automatically apply REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE unless we wire an SSLContext into TCPConnector. I suspect our async client path for non-default base_url/proxy doesn't pass the ctx through.

jisoo (eng): Reproduced on Win10 + py3.11. Our Async client builds: 
```
connector = aiohttp.TCPConnector(limit=100)
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=connector)
# we never pass ssl=ssl_ctx here
```
When proxy is present, aiohttp's proxy handling changes TLS flow and our missing ssl context means it falls back to system/openssl defaults which on some windows VMs lack the corporate root.

leo (py-sdk): Fix proposal: add explicit params to RedwoodAsyncClient signature: `trust_bundle: Optional[str]=None` and `ssl_context: Optional[ssl.SSLContext]=None` (typing import). Behavior: if ssl_context provided -> use it; elif trust_bundle provided -> ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=trust_bundle); elif env REDWOOD_TRUST_BUNDLE/REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE set -> use that; else -> ctx = ssl.create_default_context(); on Windows call ctx.load_default_certs(); finally pass ctx into aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ctx). Document precedence.

omar (infra): +1. Also add support for container friendly path and expanduser(). Make sure we don't silently swallow invalid path errors. Fail fast with a clear error message.

jisoo (eng): Tests: add a unit that constructs client with a fake CA file and asserts the connector has ssl attribute set; add an integration in CI that runs on Windows runner with a tiny MITM proxy using our CA to assert failure->success path.

nina (devex): Customer confirmed a workaround by creating their own session with a custom ssl context: 
```
import ssl
import aiohttp
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient
ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
ctx.load_verify_locations(r"C:\\corp\\proxy_ca.pem")
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ctx))
client = RedwoodAsyncClient(base_url="https://dedicated.customer.redwood.ai", session=session)
await client.chat.completions.create(...)
```
They don't want that complexity for onboarding; they'd prefer a client param.

leo (py-sdk): API name note: prefer `trust_bundle` or `cafile` to match other libs. Also add `REDWOOD_TRUST_BUNDLE` env var for parity. Update stub types for mypy: `ssl_context: Optional["ssl.SSLContext"]` if we need forward refs.

omar (infra): I'll open the GH issue and include a PR checklist: tests, docs, changelog, windows CI matrix item, and a sample snippet for onboarding.

ci-bot: Created issue redwood/redwood-py#503: "async client: accept trust_bundle / ssl_context, honor env, handle Windows cert store" (opened by omar).

nina (devex): Linking back to support TICKET-1198 so we can keep the customer updated. Thanks all :thumbsup:
